subject: Interim advisory: June 5 transient slowdown impacting chat streaming (Acme AI)
thread_body:
From: Jake Dunn <jake.dunn@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed slowdown in chat streaming during prod peak

Hi Marissa,

Heads up — between ~08:40–09:00 PDT today our users saw long pauses during streaming chat responses (UI spinner ~8–12s mid-response). This showed up across several accounts and is reproducible from our staging calls to your streaming endpoint with ~5–10% traffic.

Can you confirm whether this is on your side or if we should re-route? We're seeing elevated error budgets for streaming sessions and some timeouts in the client.

Thanks,
Jake
Product Ops | Acme AI

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Dunn <jake.dunn@acme.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed slowdown in chat streaming during prod peak

Jake —

Thanks for the report and the reproduction steps. We started an internal incident immediately and I looped in Monica (CS), Vivek (Escalations), and Engineering. Short update: we see elevated tail latency on the streaming proxy layer that correlates with increased concurrent prefix lengths from some long-conversation sessions.

Immediate ask: can you share a sanitized example session id or a short HAR of your client call? That will help us correlate requests.

I'll follow up with action items within 30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption.

—Marissa
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Acme chat slowdown — coordination + suggested mitigations

Team —

Update from infra: proxy queuing increased when multiple long-lived streams request KV cache warmups simultaneously; this pushed some requests past our streaming SLOs. Engineering is investigating a kernel-level scheduling path and will push a targeted rule change tonight.

Customer-facing mitigations we can offer to Acme now:
- Temporarily set streaming chunk_size to 512 tokens (from 1024) to reduce per-chunk processing time.
- Enable fallback to polling for sessions that exceed 10s of idle between tokens (client-side change).
- Pin requests to the model variant m-redwood-small-ff16 for their lower latency profile while we stabilize the streaming path.

I'll draft a short advisory and include concrete curl examples.

-Monica
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Internal: Acme chat slowdown — coordination + suggested mitigations

Quick engineering readout:
- Root cause (preliminary): a scheduling regression in the streaming proxy for long-prefix KV cache warmups under specific concurrency patterns. Not a model runtime regression.
- Short-term rollout: ramp new proxy rule that prioritizes streaming token flushes; expected to reduce tail by ~40% when rolled to edge nodes.
- Workaround for customers: route affected traffic to the dedicated inference pool (if available) or use model variant with smaller per-token compute.

I will post the deployment plan to INF-5123 and schedule a canary for 16:30 PDT today. Also attaching a short timeline snapshot.

—Vivek
Sr. Engineering Manager, Production Runtime

Attachment: [redwood_incident_summary_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Dunn <jake.dunn@acme.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 7 Jun 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Follow-up & post-incident guidance: June 5 streaming slowdown (Acme)

Hi Jake —

This is the formal follow-up after our incident on June 5. Thank you for the session id and for working with us during the window. Below is a concise summary, what we did, and recommended next steps for you.

Summary:
- Impact window: 2026-06-05 08:38–09:03 PDT (observed in both hosted and dedicated endpoints for a subset of long-stream sessions).
- Symptom: intermittent multi-second pauses mid-stream (8–12s tail pauses) for ~6% of streaming requests across your org.
- Root cause (confirmed): streaming proxy scheduling regression interacting with concurrent KV cache warmup patterns.

Actions we took (timeline):
- 09:05 PDT: scoped incident and mapped affected edge nodes.
- 09:30 PDT: rolled temporary proxy rule to edge canary — measurable tail improvement.
- 11:00 PDT: rolled to full edge fleet with mitigations in place.
- 16:30 PDT: deployed further prioritization fixes (INF-5123).

Customer-facing mitigations you can apply now (recommended order):
1) Pin a small fraction (~5–10%) of traffic to the lower-latency variant m-redwood-small-ff16 for sessions with >5000 token prefixes.
2) Reduce streaming chunk_size to 512 tokens; client example below:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"m-redwood-small-ff16","streaming":{"chunk_size":512,"idle_timeout_ms":10000}}'

3) If you see a token gap >10s, use a client fallback to polling generation for that session: stop the stream and fire a single non-streaming /generate call.

Longer-term work (what we're shipping):
- Full proxy scheduler rewrite to be released in Q3 (will eliminate regression class).
- Better telemetry surfaced to customers showing per-session prefix-length distribution in Console.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute runbook review with your SREs this week to walk the curl examples and help configure a safe traffic split. I can set the invite — options: Tue 10am PT or Wed 2pm PT.

Again — sorry about the disruption. We've tracked this to INF-5123 and will send an update to the public status page when the changelist lands.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
